text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro of Italy arrived in Budapest on Tuesday for an official visit. @

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn told a regular monthly press conference that the government had not violated the law in settling new energy prices and has held continuous consultations with energy suppliers.
- MPs accepted proposals for amending the new constitutional draft, bill on conflicts of interest and next year's budget. Parliament amended the act on public finances.

- Foreign Ministry spokesman announced that Premier Horn is to attend Saturday's European Council summit in Dublin. Hans van den Broek, European Commission member, will visit Hungary on December 19-20. @
- Minister of Industry, Trade and Tourism Szabolcs Fazekas is negotiating in Singapore with trade ministers from states which have filed complaints against Hungarian agricultural export subsidies.

- Outgoing National Bank vice presidents Sandor Czirjak and Frigyes Harshegyi were responsible for losses the state incurred due to the modification of a contract concluded with Creditanstalt Investment Ltd., the Supervisory Board has concluded. @
- The chemical giant TVK has bought its own shares constituting an 11.6 percent stake in the firm outside the stock exchange.
- Mark Jennings, director of British-American Tobacco in Hungary, was awarded the Order of the Republic of Hungary by President Arpad Goncz yesterday.
KOSSUTH RADIO
- Parliament ratified the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty late Tuesday night.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- Minister of Transport Karoly Lotz was elected 1997 chairman of Eurocontrol in Brussels on Tuesday.
- Several leading officials will leave the State Privatisation and Holding Co. by January 1 due to the firm's restructuring and a decreased workload.
NEPSZABADSAG

- A senior Interior Ministry official said it is conceivable that the Office for Refugees and Migration will be phased out, to be replaced by an Immigration Office with wider powers including the policing of foreigners.
NAPI GAZDASAG @

- Representatives of the power plant Dunamenti Eromu and the Hungarian Energy Office are to negotiate today on the former's profit margins. The results are expected to influence possible further steps by the Belgian firm Tractabel, which threatened to sue the Hungarian state.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- A state-owned bank serving small and medium-sized enterprises may be set up as early as January.
- A similarly named Hungarian subsidiary of the Dutch Rabobank will commence operations in early 1997. @
- The mobile phone company Westel 900 Rt. signed a $170 million loan agreement with an international consortium led by Citibank and Bank America Tuesday.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
